title: Metering for interleaved chat edits and undo operations
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Users in chat experiences frequently perform inline edits, undos, or paste-replace actions that cause the client to resend partially-overlapping prompt payloads. When these flows happen concurrently across multiple devices or tabs, the current metering pipeline can double-count input tokens or misattribute output tokens (e.g., when speculative outputs are rolled back). This ticket scopes a targeted mitigation: detect interleaved edit flows and ensure deterministic single-billing semantics while preserving low-latency streaming for live UIs.
acceptance_criteria: Server-side meter shows no duplicate charges for a user editing the most-recent-turn within 60s when client flags it as 'edit' and sends overlap token ranges
Client test harness that simulates: (a) local undo, (b) parallel edit from another tab, and (c) paste-replace mid-stream — all produce exactly one billed request per effective turn in the ledger
End-to-end integration test covering websocket reconnect + edit replay that preserves original token ledger ordering
Dashboard anomaly query that detects >0.2% duplicate-input-billing rate in the next 4 weeks after rollout
technical_notes: Add an edit_id + base_cursor metadata header on chat-turn payloads. Edit_id is client-supplied opaque UUID; base_cursor is server-assigned sequence pointer for the last-accepted turn.

Metering flow: when an edit payload has edit_id seen before within 2 minutes, treat it as idempotent and dedupe by (user_id, edit_id) at the ingestion layer rather than at final ledger commit to minimize latency.

For overlapping ranges (client does not provide exact token ranges), compute a content-based short fingerprint (SHA256 truncated to 8 bytes) at the edge to help dedupe without full tokenization on ingress.

Speculative outputs that are later rolled back by client should be marked with provisional=true in billing records; only finalized=true entries update the canonical ledger. Implement a short-lived provisional window (30s) with garbage collection rules.

Edge-case tradeoff: short fingerprint dedupe can have false positives in high-volume copy/paste scenarios; mitigation is to require fingerprint + small overlap heuristic or fall back to full tokenization in the rare conflict path.
Integrate with existing session checkpointing (see ENG-954321) to anchor edit-based dedupe during reconnects.
tests: Unit: dedupe function for (user_id, edit_id) keyed cache with TTL behavior
Integration: end-to-end harness that uses two headless browsers to perform interleaved edits and verifies billing ledger emits one canonical entry
Load: run 1k/sec simulated fine-grained edits for 30m to validate memcache sizing and false-positive rate for fingerprint dedupe
Chaos: simulate websocket reconnect immediately after an edit and ensure idempotency path prevents double-charge
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind 'edit_metering_v1' at ingestion. Deploy to staging and run regression harness.
2) Canary on 5% of traffic for two weekdays. Monitor duplicate-input-billing metric and error budget impact.
3) If stable, ramp to 50% then 100% over 72 hours. If duplicates spike >0.1% compared to baseline, roll back to previous flag state.
4) Post-rollout: keep provisional window logs for 14 days to backfill any disputes before garbage collection of provisional entries.
